sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment overlap holds at a fixed score; smooth potential-outcome means and positive one-sided support identify both traces.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine a fully explicit finite grid and estimate masses and packing counts; total clipped second-half side averages estimate the traces. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is estimated parametrically.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the pointwise minimax order \(n^{-s/(1+2s+\beta)}\) up to a slowly varying factor under regular variation.
The paper constructs an adaptive estimator attaining the pointwise rate at a degenerate-design target under inhomogeneous design.
The upper and localized lower results establish spatially varying sup-norm normalization with finitely many polynomial density zeros.
The exact minimax sup-norm constant is derived when the design density has a positive minimum.
The submanifold-integral result derives its minimax rate under a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.
The sharp boundary-effect-curve result gives pointwise and uniform location-based rates on a continuous score-density class bounded away from zero near the boundary.
Theorem 6 gives an isotropic boundary minimax result on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary.

body.tldr: A single total measurable split-sample estimator adapts to the unknown multiplicity of polynomially thin sites along an identified causal boundary trace.  A deterministic source-labeled arrangement, tie-safe mesh refinement, and upper-confidence packing count produce the first-half penalty, while zero-defined and envelope-clipped second-half side averages produce the trace estimate.  The empirical upper comparison retains its unavoidable \(1\vee J_P\) floor, and the population oracle logarithm uses the same protection.  This costs only a numerical constant and no leading global \(\log n\).  The resulting oracle inequality yields, for the same estimator, the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\); the endpoint minimax benchmarks and normalized witnesses remain attributed to the banked parent result.

project_justification.gap: Degenerate-design theory treats one point or finitely many one-dimensional zeros, while boundary-curve theory assumes density bounded away from zero.  Neither gives a total unweighted-supremum estimator that measurably learns thin-site multiplicity while remaining valid when a queried population thin set is empty.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a profile-adaptive estimator whose stochastic penalty is the protected packing entropy \(1+\log\{e(1\vee J_P)\}\) at each site's local mass severity, with every sample-dependent selection and every breakpoint tie defined on every realization.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs an explicit source-labeled first-half arrangement, proves that deterministic mesh refinement preserves every empirical pattern within distance strictly below \(h/4\), estimates the corresponding floored packing entropy, uses zero-defined clipped second-half side averages, proves a population oracle inequality with an event-explicit negligible remainder, and derives both endpoint rates from one procedure without a hidden global logarithm.

body.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) supplies the single-site bias--information equation. Gaiffas (2007), "On pointwise adaptive curve estimation based on inhomogeneous data," ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 11, pages 344--364, studies pointwise adaptation at a degenerate-design target. The distinct Statistica Sinica paper of Gaiffas (2009), volume 19, pages 427--447, establishes uniform estimation with spatial normalization for finitely many one-dimensional density zeros. Neither paper estimates boundary packing multiplicity under one unweighted supremum loss. Antoniadis, Pensky, and Sapatinas (2014) study global adaptation for inhomogeneous one-dimensional designs. Bertin (2004) gives the positive-density supremum benchmark. Xiaohong Chen and Wayne Yuan Gao (2026), Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper 2450R1 (March 2026), derive a submanifold-integral minimax rate under positive bounded design density; that scalar positive-density rate informs the geometric comparison but does not address a boundary trace with polynomial side-mass depletion. Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the causal identification logic. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu formulate location-based and distance-based boundary results on a continuous-score-density class bounded away from zero near the boundary. The first nontrivial result here is instead the profile-packing oracle inequality and its same-estimator isolated/pervasive upper-rate adaptation under polynomial two-sided depletion. The banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_uniform\_log\_penalty}\) result proves a positive-density distance-rule converse. It varies an estimator-information restriction while maintaining regular local mass, so it neither supplies nor rules out a frontier driven by the multiplicity of polynomially thin sites.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Scalar side mass does not imply coercivity of higher-order local-polynomial Gram matrices, so the estimator uses local averages. It treats \(L\) and \(\sigma\) as fixed known class constants. Constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from \(2\).
body.honest_scope: The profile-adaptive packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim.  Identification, the measurable empirical-packing comparison, and flat-law validity support that theorem.  Because \(\widehat J\geq1\) by construction whereas an empty population thin set has \(J_P=0\), the valid upper comparison and oracle entropy use \(1\vee J_P\); this protection adds only a numerical constant and does not alter either endpoint rate.  The estimator is total: empty side counts map to zero before clipping, an empty admissible set maps to \(h_0\), and the final contrast is clipped to \([-2L,2L]\).  The endpoint minimax orders belong to the banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) result; the corollary here claims only simultaneous upper-rate attainment by one estimator.  At \(\kappa=3\), the retained witness divergence is \(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\).  Formally setting \(\kappa=2\) in the balances recovers the bivariate Lipschitz pointwise rate \(n^{-1/4}\) and uniform rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), without uniform constants at that excluded endpoint.
